explanation: In the UK, especially in business and professional settings, moderate direct eye contact is expected and reads as honest, confident, and engaged; avoiding it can come across as evasive. Constant, unbroken staring can feel intense or confrontational, so natural breaks in gaze during conversation are normal.
local_tip: Hold steady, natural eye contact when speaking or listening, glancing away periodically rather than staring fixedly.

also_check.note: Prolonged direct eye contact, especially with someone senior, can be seen as disrespectful; brief glances are preferred.
Direct eye contact between men can signal sincerity, but is often reduced between genders out of modesty.
Similarly values direct eye contact as a sign of confidence and honesty, closely matching UK norms.
